activities.anchor: is land and everything permanently attached
activities.caption: file each item under the right property class
activities.name: rePropSort

config.prompt: The law's first sorting problem — real or personal?

items.label: the soil and minerals beneath (unless separately sold)
appurtenances — rights that run with the land
a debt, a patent, a copyright — intangible but owned and transferable
the picked ear of corn a tenant harvests

config.why: The growing corn is real property, the picked ear a chattel — the boundary sounds clean until objects move across it, which is the fixture problem.

activities.anchor: if it is bolted down, it is part of the house
activities.caption: true or false — the fixture tests
activities.name: reFixtureJudge

statements.s: Method of attachment is only the first of the MARIA tests.
statements.why: Adaptability, relationship of the parties, intention and express agreement follow — attachment alone is not decisive.

statements.s: A business tenant's bolted-down trade fixtures remain the tenant's personal property.
statements.why: Provided they are removed before the lease ends and any damage repaired — the dentist's chair goes with the dentist.

statements.s: Crops grown by a tenant become the landlord's real property.
statements.why: Emblements stay personal property with a right to harvest — the growing corn is real, the picked ear is a chattel.

statements.s: The professional reflex is to resolve fixtures in the written contract.
statements.why: Not in the doorway argument at handover — which is why purchase contracts list exclusions in writing.

activities.anchor: Ownership is legally described by its
activities.caption: file each estate under its family
activities.name: reEstateSort

config.prompt: The estate families — file each by duration:

items.label: fee simple absolute — the full bundle, of indefinite duration, freely inheritable
fee simple defeasible — ends or reverts if a stated condition is broken
the life estate — for a named person's lifetime, then to the remainderman
estate for years — a fixed term
tenancy at sufferance — the holdover tenant

config.why: Valuation follows the estate, not the dirt: a 99-year leasehold flat and a freehold flat on identical land are different assets with different prices.

activities.anchor: Several people can hold the same estate
activities.caption: pair each ownership form with its rule
activities.name: reCoownMatch

config.prompt: Forms of holding — pair each with its decisive rule:

pairs.right: possibly unequal shares; a deceased share passes to heirs; any co-owner may sell without permission
the four unities plus right of survivorship — the deceased share vanishes into the survivors
the married-couple variant, in some states
fee simple ownership of a unit plus shared ownership of common elements
a corporation owns the building; residents own shares and a proprietary lease

config.why: Two siblings as joint tenants: one dies, the survivor owns the whole. As tenants in common, the half goes to her heirs — who may be strangers to the survivor.

activities.anchor: is the right to use another
activities.caption: find the faulty line — an easements briefing
activities.name: reLicenceSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on easements is wrong — click it:
lines: Easements are created expressly in writing, by implication, by necessity, or by prescription.
Prescription requires open, notorious, hostile and continuous use for the statutory period.
The same elements make adverse possession, which can ripen into ownership itself.
A licence is the stronger instrument — it binds successors and runs with the land.
config.correction: A licence is the easement's weaker cousin — mere revocable permission, your cinema ticket — and must not be confused with it.
config.why: An appurtenant easement runs with the land (dominant and servient estates); a licence can be withdrawn tomorrow.

activities.anchor: that adverse possession rewards a stealthy squatter
activities.caption: fill the blanks — what actually ripens
activities.name: reAdverseCloze

config.text: The doctrine requires the opposite of stealth: the use must be %%0%%, notorious and hostile — and what actually ripens into a right is the owner's long %%1%% in the face of visible use.
config.hint: The fence built in plain sight, the driveway driven every day — and what the owner did about it for years.

activities.anchor: Two worked miniatures show the doctrine priced in practice
activities.caption: call the foreclosure surplus
activities.name: reLienEst

config.prompt: A house worth 400,000 dollars carries a 300,000-dollar first mortgage and a 50,000-dollar second mortgage. Roughly how much surplus remains for the junior claimants?
config.why: Foreclosure distributes by priority, not size: the first mortgagee is paid in full, the second takes what remains of the 100,000-dollar surplus — and the mechanics' lien holder may find itself paid from dregs or nothing.

activities.anchor: Three deeper layers show where the foundation leads
activities.caption: drag the divider — recording versus registration
activities.name: reRecordingCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to make title provable — drag the divider.

before.label: Anglo-American recording
before.text: Title a matter of traced documents and priority rules — first to record wins, subject to exceptions.

after.label: Torrens registration
after.text: Title conclusive by state guarantee (Australia and scattered jurisdictions).

config.why: The choice of system shapes everything from conveyancing cost to fraud risk — and the severed-rights and regulatory-takings questions keep the bundle metaphor a working legal instrument.
